title: Seat a swivelling ball stud square in a knuckle's tapered hole, from a tie rod that swings
instruction: Lift the outer end of the tie rod off its wooden block, hold its swinging ball stud upright over the steering knuckle's tapered hole, push the stud straight down until its taper seats in the hole, then let go and lift the gripper clear.
context: ATRO Steer King Universal Tie Rods, Installation Instructions, step 7: "Insert a stud into the tapered hole of the Steering Knuckle. Install the Castle Nut loosely on the thread." Step 1 gives the cost of a bad seat: a hole "damaged or oblong/oval, allowing the new stud to rock in the hole" means the knuckle must be replaced, and "may result in a stud fracture and partial loss of steering." https://www.atrobushing.com/documents/EN-Steer-King-Tie-Rods-Installation-Instructions.pdf Home is MOOG's hand test fit: the clean stud "should seat firmly without rocking". https://www.moogparts.com/content/dam/marketing/North-America/moog/pdf/tech-tips/proper-ball-joint-stud-nut-torquing-tech-tip.pdf Done by: automotive and truck service technicians (steering and suspension).
setup: The two arm bases stand 61 cm apart on an oak table. The left end of a car's steering rack is fixed 25 cm out from the bases and 12 cm left of the midline: an aluminium tube 44 mm across on a 50 x 100 mm stand, with a rubber boot. A steel tie rod, 16 mm across and 36 cm long, hangs from the rack's inner ball joint 14.1 cm above the table and runs to the right. Near its outer end it rests level on a wooden block, 40 x 30 x 130 mm, 17 cm right of the midline. The outer tie rod end is a black body 22 mm across and a socket housing 40 mm across and 35 mm tall, 24 cm right of the midline, with a steel ball stud hanging straight down from it on its ball. The stud's taper is 18.0 mm across at its large end and 14.7 mm at its small end over 19.3 mm, with a 13.5 mm thread 22 mm long below. The stud swivels up to 20 degrees each way about two axes, and the tie rod turns up, down and sideways on the inner joint. The moving parts weigh 170 g. A fixed cast-iron steering knuckle has its hole 31.9 cm out and 23.3 cm right: an upright 30 x 80 x 140 mm and a steering arm, 24 x 16 mm, ending in a boss 44 mm across with a tapered hole that matches the stud, its axis upright and its top 90.6 mm above the table.
scoring: Home, as on the real parts: where the matched stud stops when pushed by hand into the clean, dry hole (MOOG test fit), read as the thread's protrusion below the steering arm's bottom face with a caliper depth rod; 22.6 mm for this sim's stud and hole. Seated: protrusion within 0.5 mm of home, the taper's large end within 1 mm of the hole's axis, the stud's axis within 2 degrees of the hole's. Clear: no part of either arm within 10 mm of the tie rod, its outer end or the stud. Still: the taper and the rod's outer end under 0.01 m/s and 0.5 rad/s. 1.0 when seated, still and clear for 1 s, which ends the trial. 0.8 when seated, still and clear at the last step but not for 1 s. 0.6 when seated at the last step but moving or not clear (a hand still on the tie rod). 0.3 when the threaded tip is at least 2 mm below the hole's top, the stud's axis is within 2.42 mm of the hole's at the hole's top, the protrusion is at most home plus 0.5 mm, and the stud is within 2 degrees of upright. 0 otherwise: beside the hole, on its rim, cocked more than 2 degrees, dropped, or at the start.
reset_notes: Lift the stud out of the knuckle, let it hang straight down, and lay the tie rod's outer end back on its block.
fidelity: Taper as four short cylinders just inside the cone, hole as 24 flats: the stud seats 0.6 mm past flush, so home is 22.6 mm and 0.6 mm of taper shows under the arm (real matched parts show only thread). Ball joints are damped hinges, no preload. 170 g moving, against about 1.2 kg solid steel. Knuckle fixed, friction 1.2/1.0; stud 0.5/0.4. No nut or thread. Rod length, ball to taper, swivel range, thread length, housing and knuckle body are estimates.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (2,400 steps, re-run on this final fixture with the corrected stud neck and the let-go check); demo: 1.0 (success at 21.35 s, step 427)
